title: Keep young children alive: which implementable measures work beyond what a country's income and setting predict

SH.IMM.IDPT.solution: Routine childhood immunization (DTP3 coverage) delivered through existing primary care
SH.IMM.IDPT.implement: Sustain cold chain, reliable vaccine supply and outreach sessions; track coverage by district and chase dropouts.
SH.IMM.IDPT.who: Ministries of health with Gavi-style financing, NGOs running outreach
SH.IMM.IDPT.first_test: Pick two low-coverage districts, add monthly outreach and dropout tracing for 6 months, compare DTP3 coverage with matched districts.

SH.STA.BASS.ZS.solution: Basic sanitation access (safely managed toilets and hygiene)
SH.STA.BASS.ZS.implement: Subsidized household latrines plus behaviour-change and local maintenance; pair with water treatment.
SH.STA.BASS.ZS.who: Municipal water and sanitation authorities, community-led total sanitation programs
SH.STA.BASS.ZS.first_test: Roll out in one sub-district with a village-level sanitation committee; compare diarrhoeal admissions against a matched sub-district after a year.

SH.MED.PHYS.ZS.solution: Frontline clinical coverage (physicians and trained community health workers)
SH.MED.PHYS.ZS.implement: Train, pay and supervise community health workers with a clear package of treatments and referral.
SH.MED.PHYS.ZS.who: Ministries of health, health-worker training institutions, NGO program partners
SH.MED.PHYS.ZS.first_test: Deploy supervised community health workers in one catchment; compare under-five treatment rates and referrals with a comparable catchment.

SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS.solution: Dedicated public financing for primary care and child health
SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS.implement: Ring-fence a budget line for primary care with transparent disbursement to facilities.
SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS.who: Finance and health ministries, donors pooling funds
SH.XPD.CHEX.GD.ZS.first_test: Ring-fence funds for primary care in one region; compare facility stock-outs and child outcomes after two budget cycles.

statement: Children under five die of causes that known, deliverable measures prevent. Which of those measures are worth a foundation or government implementing first?
